messages:
alex: Heads-up — apac-ne1 GPU pool showing KV cache OOMs and node flapping since 02:03 UTC. p95 gen latency +22%, 3% 5xxs on /v1/generate.
ops-bot: [ALERT] region=apac-ne1 component=gpu-pool severity=high metric=p95_latency value=220ms
maya: I'm on it, starting a selective drain of unhealthy nodes in apac-gpu-3, will keep a subset warm.
tolga: recommend gradual GSLB steer rather than full cutover. Can we do: apac->30, eu->50, na->20 with 20s TTL and 10% canary immediately? That avoids cold-start stampede.
jia: FYI runtime: moving load to EU will bump KV cache miss rate initially. If we can prewarm the most common prefixes in eu pools it helps. I can trigger prewarm job for top-100 prefixes.
sam: I can run the gslb change. Command I'll run: `gslbctl adjust-weights --set apac=30,eu=50,na=20 --ttl 20 --canary 10`
alex: good. also set routing fallback policy to prefer be-conservative on capacity so we're not overloading eu.
sam: executing now.
deploy-bot: gslbctl change accepted: change_id=chg-20260318-01 state=applying
sam: change applied. monitoring metrics.
ops-bot: [INFO] gslb change chg-20260318-01 applied. new_weights={apac:30,eu:50,na:20} ttl=20s
alex: initial telemetry: apac p95 down to +8% above baseline, eu p95 increased +40ms, error rate in eu still within SLO.
maya: Drain in apac completed on 6/8 nodes, leaving 2 warm nodes. health checks ok on those.
jia: prewarm job started for eu top prefixes. I'll post completion in 5m.
product-ops: Heads-up product teams — internal incident, no customer-facing outage yet. We're monitoring. :eyes:
on-call-sre: keeping a 15min canary window, if no error spike we'll increase apac->15, eu->60, na->25.
tolga: note on costs: steering to eu will increase inter-region egress by ~10-15% for API-heavy customers — flag to finance if this persists. :money_with_wings:
jia: prewarm complete. cache hitrate in eu up ~12% after warm.
ops-bot: [METRIC] region=eu cache_hitrate delta=+12%
alex: canary period passed 12/15min — no regressions. proceeding with ramp. Sam, please apply next weights.
sam: applying ramp to apac=15, eu=60, na=25. `gslbctl adjust-weights --set apac=15,eu=60,na=25 --ttl 30`
deploy-bot: gslbctl change accepted: change_id=chg-20260318-02 state=applying
ops-bot: [INFO] gslb change chg-20260318-02 applied. new_weights={apac:15,eu:60,na:25} ttl=30s
alex: metrics: apac latency stabilized near baseline for remaining warm nodes, eu latency within expected increase but error rate steady. No user-facing impact reported.
maya: troubleshooting summary: root cause likely packet loss toward a subset of apac-ne1 leaf switches causing sporadic node flaps. Networking team engaged for hardware replacement; ETA ~3 hours.
tolga: recommended follow-ups: 1) add auto-prefill for EU when apac eviction event detected, 2) tune GSLB auto-steer policy to prefer gradual 20% steps, 3) post-incident cost delta report.
product-ops: Please draft a short internal postmortem for customers once we have root cause and timeline.
on-call-sre: I'll keep the routing policy in this state for next 4 hours and hand off to day shift. If apac stabilizes and we get healthy node count +70% we can move weights back slowly.
alex: thanks team — good coordination. Action items: maya to confirm hardware replacement timeline, tolga to open cost impact issue, jia to add prewarm as automated response, sam to document gslb change ids.
maya: confirmed replacement ticket open with network; tech onsite ETA 2.5h.
ops-bot: [RESOLVED] incident state=mitigated region=apac-ne1 routing=partial-steer
